name: Supply Chain
title: Supplier disruption response planning
summary: Connect supplier incidents to material demand, qualified alternatives, and planner-approved recovery scenarios.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A machinery manufacturer receives notice that a supplier cannot deliver a critical bearing on time. Procurement, production planning, and engineering need a shared view of affected assemblies and feasible responses. Agents prepare scenarios; planners and engineering owners authorize sourcing and schedule changes.
problem: Supplier messages use inconsistent part descriptions and uncertain dates. A superficially cheaper substitute may lack engineering approval, and a rescheduled purchase order may disrupt another plant. Local optimization can therefore hide enterprise-wide constraints.
whyAgents: Specialists map supply exposure, inspect approved alternatives, simulate planning scenarios, and prepare supplier questions. Structured optimization and material requirements calculations remain deterministic, with agents interpreting exceptions and explaining scenario assumptions.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Evaluate the completeness and usability of recovery options before attributing service-level improvements. Record where human negotiation, engineering qualification, or physical capacity constrained the result so agent quality is measured separately.

agents.name: Exposure mapper
agents.responsibility: Trace late material to purchase orders, inventory, and dependent assemblies.
agents.boundary: Cannot change demand or assume unrecorded substitute equivalence.

agents.name: Qualification investigator
agents.responsibility: Retrieve engineering-approved substitute parts and supplier qualification status.
agents.boundary: Cannot approve a new supplier or technical substitution.

agents.name: Scenario planner
agents.responsibility: Run bounded shortage, transfer, and schedule scenarios with explicit assumptions.
agents.boundary: Cannot commit purchase orders or production schedules.

agents.name: Procurement briefing agent
agents.responsibility: Compile supplier questions and compare scenario evidence for buyers.
agents.boundary: Cannot promise volumes, accept terms, or contact suppliers without approval.

systems.name: ERP and planning platform
systems.role: Authoritative demand, stock, purchase orders, and scenario calculations.

systems.name: Product lifecycle and quality systems
systems.role: Define engineering substitutions, effective revisions, and supplier qualifications.

systems.name: Supplier collaboration portal
systems.role: Stores authenticated disruption notices and approved communications separately from agent-generated drafts.

flow.title: Register disruption
flow.description: Authenticate the supplier event, map supplier part numbers, and record uncertain delivery windows without choosing a convenient date.

flow.title: Calculate exposure
flow.description: Read a consistent planning snapshot and identify assemblies, plants, and customer commitments that depend on the material.

flow.title: Check alternatives
flow.description: Filter candidate substitutes by engineering approval, effective revision, qualification, and available capacity.

flow.title: Simulate responses
flow.description: Evaluate approved alternatives, transfers, and schedule changes with deterministic constraints and clearly labeled scenario assumptions.

flow.title: Review cross-plant effects
flow.description: Show planners which shortages move elsewhere and which assumptions remain unconfirmed before a buyer authorizes action.

flow.title: Commit selected plan
flow.description: Revalidate inventory and order versions, submit approved changes through ERP adapters, and monitor supplier acknowledgement separately from execution.

failures.scenario: A substitute is approved for an older assembly revision only.
failures.detection: Qualification lookup conflicts with the current bill-of-materials revision.
failures.recovery: Remove that scenario and request engineering assessment without inventing equivalence.

failures.scenario: Two plants reserve the same emergency inventory.
failures.detection: Reservation conflict or changed available-to-promise quantity rejects the second plan.
failures.recovery: Recalculate both affected scenarios using the current allocation and return ownership to planners.

controls: Use governed part identifiers and engineering revision checks before scenario generation.
Keep optimization assumptions and supplier-confirmed commitments visibly separate.
Require buyer approval for commercial commitments and engineering approval for substitutions.
Reserve scarce inventory atomically before publishing a committed recovery plan.
Restrict supplier pricing and contracts to authorized procurement teams.

metrics.name: Exposure completeness
metrics.definition: Known affected demand lines captured in the disruption graph divided by audited affected demand lines.

metrics.name: Scenario preparation latency
metrics.definition: Time from authenticated notice to planner-reviewable options with current constraints.

metrics.name: Assumption closure
metrics.definition: Unconfirmed scenario assumptions resolved before commitment divided by assumptions requiring confirmation.

metrics.name: Plan invalidation rate
metrics.definition: Approved scenarios requiring revision because source constraints changed divided by approved scenarios.

tradeoffs.cost: Depends on accurate bills of material and identifier mapping.

tradeoffs.benefit: Controls planning cost and review complexity.
tradeoffs.cost: May omit creative alternatives outside approved candidate sets.
Recovery speed depends on both review queues.

rollout.acceptance: Planners verify affected assemblies and reject unqualified substitutes across representative incidents.
One material family compares proposed options with planner decisions and tests commercial-data access boundaries.
Approved changes launch after inventory-contention, stale-plan, and supplier-acknowledgement recovery pass.
